brief_rationale: The trajectory met the responsibility chain: the doctor recognized the post–mid-trimester-induction stage, actively checked/triaged bleeding and systemic red flags, safely separated aspirin/heparin from levothyroxine, used/asked for records, and created a concrete obstetric follow-up plan with receipt. There was no serious or minor in-chain error visible; the patient ultimately confirmed the medication plan, emergency thresholds, and follow-up timing. High-order credit is warranted for dynamic reprioritization to urgent in-person obstetric assessment, verification of ambiguous immune/thyroid/genetic implications, and bounded closure carrying residual pathology/genetic uncertainty forward. Therefore the deterministic boundary is Perfect.

closure_assessment.explanation: The episode closed safely after in-person obstetric review: the patient knew not to self-restart aspirin/heparin, to continue levothyroxine with thyroid follow-up, to monitor bleeding, and to return urgently for defined symptoms while awaiting pathology/genetic results.
